**Visual Analysis:**

- **Plant part**: Tomato leaves (compound leaf, characteristic shape)
- **Key features**:
  - White to grayish powdery coating covering the upper leaf surface
  - Leaves remain mostly green but with dusty/chalky patches spread across the surface
  - No dark necrotic concentric rings (rules out Early Blight)
  - No water-soaked lesions or brown/black blotches (rules out Late Blight, Bacterial diseases)
  - No mosaic/mottled yellowing pattern (rules out viral diseases)
  - No obvious stem collapse or wilting (rules out wilt diseases)

**Reasoning:**

The distinctive white powdery coating on the upper leaf surface is the hallmark of **Powdery Mildew**. This fungal disease produces superficial mycelium and conidia that appear as a white to grayish powder on leaf surfaces. The leaves are still structurally intact and green underneath, which is consistent with early-to-mid stage powdery mildew. This pattern does not match Leaf Mold (which shows yellow spots above and olive mold below) or Gray Mold (which causes gray fuzzy growth typically on damaged/senescent tissue).
